questions.q: What does the COMFY acronym stand for?
a: Calmness, openness, movement, fun and your passions
Calm, optimism, mindfulness, fitness and yearning
Clarity, order, movement, focus and yielding
Comfort, openness, meals, fitness and youth
questions.why: The overview lists the five morning ingredients Gross builds his routine around.

questions.q: How does Gross suggest you begin the day?
a: With a calming activity such as meditation and breathing
By checking email before you get out of bed
By exercising before doing anything else
By writing a long to-do list for the day
questions.why: The first lesson says jumping straight from a buzzing alarm into work is a recipe for anxiety.

questions.q: What does the openness step involve?
a: Connecting with others and journaling about your thoughts
Sharing every private detail publicly
Accepting every invitation that comes your way
Saying yes to as many commitments as possible
questions.why: The first lesson suggests texting an old friend, thanking someone or being vulnerable in a journal.

questions.q: Why does Gross include something funny in the morning?
a: Laughter reduces worry and keeps you in the present
It improves your performance during workouts
It makes you answer emails faster
It can replace meditation entirely
questions.why: The second lesson recommends building a Positive News Network or sharing jokes with a funny buddy.

questions.q: What does feeling young and thinking old mean?
a: Recall childhood joys while dropping immature mindsets
Exercise like a child and plan like an elder
Keep childish habits and avoid responsibility
Act younger than your age at work
questions.why: The third lesson says this helps you break social pressure and pursue what actually makes you tick.
